provider.name: Plants of the World Online
provider.organization_type: global plant taxonomy, nomenclature, accepted-name, synonymy, classification, distribution, trait, use, bibliography, download, and scientific-reference infrastructure
provider.description: Plants of the World Online is a Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew resource providing global plant taxonomy and distribution information, integrating accepted names, synonyms, IPNI LSIDs, WCVP taxonomy and geography, descriptions, traits, uses, references, and images.
institutional_context: Herbaria, botanical gardens, taxonomic specialists, floras, monographs, and checklist partners

purpose.summary: Crawl-ready source catalog for POWO documentation, taxonomy, nomenclature, WCVP, IPNI, distributions, descriptions, traits, uses, references, images, APIs, downloads, schemas, editorial workflows, data quality, rights, software, standards, and related authorities.
purpose.authoritative_notice: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, POWO, WCVP, IPNI, official downloads and documentation, source publications, specialist decisions, and cited authorities remain authoritative for names, status, identifiers, geography, versions, rights, and contacts.

review.notes: Primary POWO portal for accepted plant names, synonyms, classification, distributions, descriptions, traits, uses, images, and references.

notes: Verify whether POWO exposes a supported public API, bulk export, GraphQL, SPARQL, or OAI-PMH interface and identify canonical routes.
Verify authentication, endpoint names, methods, parameters, response schemas, pagination, rate limits, and deprecations.
Do not infer undocumented editorial or administrative services from browser traffic.
Do not store credentials, API keys, cookies, tokens, or session identifiers in this manifest.
Capture exact POWO, Kew, WCVP, IPNI, image, download, API, source-dataset, and third-party legal wording.
Separate taxonomic facts from descriptions, uses, images, distribution data, source publications, and software.
Preserve taxon ID, IPNI LSID, accepted-name ID, source dataset and version, citation, access date, license URI, rights holder, and provenance.
Do not assume all images, descriptive text, use statements, or third-party datasets share the same rights as name and classification facts.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
POWO routes, WCVP and IPNI products, API availability, downloads, schemas, taxonomic coverage, and legal pages may change; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every POWO taxon page, IPNI name record, WCVP row, image, reference, API result, or download record when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store credentials, API keys, passwords, cookies, tokens, private editorial notes, unpublished corrections, or session identifiers in this JSON file.
Taxonomic facts, nomenclatural records, distributions, descriptions, traits, uses, images, source datasets, API output, downloads, and software may carry different rights.

Always preserve POWO taxon ID, IPNI LSID, accepted-name ID, scientific name, authorship, rank, parent, classification, taxonomic and nomenclatural status, synonyms, publication, type data, TDWG distribution, native and introduced status, descriptions, traits, uses, references, source dataset and version, release version, citation, rights, source URL, and provenance.
